reasons.correctness_risk: The core rules look right: the remainder goes to the first-listed members, exact shares must sum to cents, settlement is greedy with first-listed ties, and commits are serialized copy-on-write, published only after the rename succeeds. The risks: it rejects a member list with duplicates even when it holds two distinct names, it adds extra 400s for very long IDs and huge balances, and its intricate number-source code has a regex fallback that never runs on current Node.
reasons.structure: Pure helpers for validation, balances, settlement and persistence, a createService factory that takes its data file and starting state, and a clean promise-chain commit queue. Some extras the request did not ask for, such as a header size derived from ID lengths, add moving parts.
reasons.readability: Good names, but dense and clever in places: number source text is re-parsed with a regex fallback, isWholeCent does decimal-place arithmetic, and encodedGroupIdLength doubles as a validity check by returning 0.
reasons.error_handling: Very thorough: fatal UTF-8 decoding, whole-cent checks on the number as written in the request, full validation of the saved ledger with a fail-fast start, temp-file cleanup, failed saves leave memory unchanged, request errors are handled and bodies drained. Gaps: no body-size limit, and error responses have no body.
reasons.tests: Broad and precise: remainder, exact, zero and omitted shares, invalid inputs that do not use up a number, ties including unsorted numeric names, prototype-like keys, concurrent creates and expenses, restarts in most tests, and an injected rename failure. Some tests are tied to fs.rename and the file format, and a few malformed-body cases do not check the status.

reasons.correctness_risk: Small and correct for the request: shares stored by member index, BigInt balances, first-listed ties, and no lost updates because everything after the body read is synchronous. The risks: it needs a recent Node without saying so (JSON.rawJSON runs on every balances and settlements response), it rejects whitespace-only names, it checks for 409 before validating members, and its atomicity depends on an unenforced rule that a future await would silently break.
reasons.structure: Compact, with pure balance and settlement helpers. But env parsing and data loading happen at module level, the groups map is a mutable global, saveGroup both persists and publishes state, and file I/O inside request handlers is synchronous. The module cannot be imported for unit tests.
reasons.readability: Short, plainly named functions, with comments that explain the key decisions: synchronous publication, re-reading the group after the body, and bigint serialization. Easy to follow end to end.
reasons.error_handling: Good request validation: safe integers, share sums that cannot overflow, distinct non-blank names, and URI errors. Writes use a temp file and rename with cleanup, and failures return 500 with a JSON error body. But the saved ledger is trusted without validation, there is no body-size limit, and only error.message is logged.
reasons.tests: Five dense end-to-end tests cover the remainder, exact shares, a long list of 400s with numbering kept, ties on both sides in non-alphabetical order, 32 concurrent posts with a SIGKILL restart, and a write failure tested from outside. Gaps: no test shows that PORT is used, the negative-share case is rejected by the over-sum check first so the negative check is never tested, and nothing tests concurrent creates or that a 409 keeps the original group.

why: Both build what the request asks for, but X is the safer code to accept. Its explicit commit queue copies state and publishes it only after a successful rename, it validates the saved ledger on load, and its tests are broader and sharper. Y is simpler and easier to read, but its concurrency guarantee rests on synchronous file I/O, module globals and an unenforced rule of no await after the body read; X's costs are over-engineering in places and a stricter-than-requested rule against duplicate member names.
